hero.kicker: Fall cleanup and leaf removal in Davison, MI
hero.title: Leaves vacuumed up **right from the yard.**

local.title: The city picks up leaves **on set dates.**
local.intro: Davison handles leaves two ways, and both start with you raking. In the city, the DPW runs a few sweeps each fall and asks residents to rake leaves to the curb line, leaves only. In Davison Township, leaves go out in paper bags on Tuesdays until late November.

points.title: City pickup dates
points.body: For 2026 the city planned three complete leaf pickups, the first on or before October 19, with one more in mid November only if needed. Signs go up the Friday before, and the city warns that rocks, boards and brush mixed in with the leaves damage its equipment.

points.title: East and west of M-15
points.body: Some rounds run on different weeks for each side of M-15. A big maple that drops late can miss your side's window, and MSU Extension notes that leaves left matted on a lawn smother the grass under them.

points.title: Township paper bags
points.body: Davison Township takes yard waste in brown paper bags or marked cans, each under 50 pounds, every week from the first Tuesday in April to the last Tuesday in November. A wooded acre fills a lot of bags.

points.title: Leaves are not on the burn permit
points.body: The township's burn permit covers brush, tree trimmings, shrubbery and other wood. Leaves are not on that list, so check with the township before lighting a pile, or have them hauled away.

logistics.title: How many visits a Davison yard needs.
body: It depends on the trees. Some Davison yards need one big cleanup after the branches are bare, and a heavy canopy may need a visit in late October and another in November. Rob looks at your trees and tells you which makes sense.

We blow leaves out of the beds and from under the shrubs, cut back spent perennials, run the leaf vacuum and haul everything off in our dump trailer. The last cut of the year can happen on the same visit, bagging what is left on the lawn.

faq.q: Do you do leaf removal in Davison, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes does fall cleanups and leaf removal in the City of Davison and Davison Township. We blow the leaves out of beds and off the lawn, vacuum them into our trailer and haul them away, so nothing waits at the curb.

faq.q: When does the City of Davison pick up leaves?
faq.a: The DPW posts a fall schedule every year. In 2026 the first pickup started on or before October 19, with later rounds into November and a final one only if needed. The city calls it a guide that can change with weather and workload, so check its page for the current year.

faq.q: How do I put leaves out for the city's leaf pickup?
faq.a: The city asks residents to rake leaves to the curb line once its signs are up and to keep cars off the street. Only leaves: rocks, boards and brush damage the equipment. If you would rather skip the raking, we vacuum the leaves up from the yard and take them with us.

faq.q: Are leaves bad for the lawn over winter?
faq.a: A thick layer is. MSU Extension says a mat of leaves left on turf over winter can smother it, slow green-up in spring and lead to more snow mold. A light scatter mulched with the mower is fine; a heavy drop needs to come off.
